source.title: Mastering Coding: AI and Robotics
source.note: Lesson summaries, learning points and activities are adapted from the teacher-panel Foundation 2 lesson content. Consult the supplied textbook PDF for full original context and illustrations.

chapters.title: More About a Computer
chapters.description: Explore more about a computer through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in more about a computer.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: What is a computer?
topics.content: A computer is an electronic machine that helps us perform many tasks. It accepts data, processes it, and gives useful information as output.
learning_points: A computer can perform calculations and help us create documents.
It can be used to play games, draw pictures, listen to music, and learn.
A computer is used in homes, schools, hospitals, banks, and offices.
examples: An electronic machine for many tasks.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name three tasks they have seen a computer perform.

topics.title: Types of computers
topics.content: The textbook introduces different kinds of computers, including desktop computers, laptops, and wearable computers.
learning_points: A desktop computer is usually kept on a desk and is not designed to be carried around.
A laptop is portable and can be used in different places.
Wearable computers include devices such as smart watches.
topics.activity_text: Show pictures of a desktop, laptop, tablet, and smart watch. Ask which devices are easy to carry.

topics.title: Parts of a computer
topics.content: A computer system has several parts that work together. The textbook introduces the monitor, CPU, keyboard, and mouse.
learning_points: The monitor displays information.
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) processes instructions and is often called the brain of the computer.
The keyboard is used to enter text and numbers.
The mouse is used to point, click, and select items.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to point to the monitor, CPU cabinet, keyboard, and mouse on a computer.

topics.title: Turning on a computer
topics.content: The textbook describes the basic steps for starting a computer safely.
learning_points: Make sure the computer and its connections are ready.
Switch on the main power supply and the UPS, if one is used.
Press the power button on the CPU and monitor.
Wait for the operating system and desktop to appear.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate the start-up sequence in the computer lab and ask students to put the steps in order.

topics.title: Shutting down a computer
topics.content: A computer should be shut down using the operating system so that work can close properly.
learning_points: Save your work before shutting down.
Use the Start menu and choose the Power option.
Select Shut down and wait until the computer turns off.
Do not switch off the power suddenly while the computer is working.
examples: Wait for the computer to turn off.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to arrange the shutdown steps in the correct order.

topics.title: Human vs Computer
topics.content: Humans and computers can both work with information, but they are different. Humans have feelings and natural intelligence, while computers follow instructions and process data.
learning_points: Humans can think, feel emotions, and make decisions using experience.
Computers can work quickly and accurately when given instructions.
Computers do not have human feelings.
People create instructions and decide how computers should be used.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to compare one task a person does and one task a computer does.

chapters.title: Applications of Computers
chapters.description: Explore applications of computers through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in applications of computers.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Uses of computers
topics.content: Computers are used in many everyday places and activities. They help people work, communicate, learn, and store information.
learning_points: Computers are used at home, in schools, offices, banks, shops, and hospitals.
They help people prepare documents, calculate, communicate, and find information.
Computers can support learning and entertainment.
topics.activity_text: Name places shown in the chapter and explain one way a computer is used at each place.

topics.title: Applications of a computer
topics.content: The chapter describes practical applications of computers in areas such as education, business, communication, healthcare, transport, and public services.
learning_points: Computers help students learn and teachers prepare learning materials.
Businesses use computers for records, billing, and communication.
Hospitals use computers to maintain patient information and support medical work.
Computers help people communicate and access information.
topics.activity_text: Give students everyday situations and ask which computer application could help.

topics.title: Advantages
topics.content: Computers offer several advantages when they are used appropriately.
learning_points: Speed: computers can process information quickly.
Accuracy: they can produce accurate results when correct data and instructions are supplied.
Storage: they can store large amounts of information.
Diligence: they can repeat tasks without getting tired in the way people do.
Versatility: they can be used for many different kinds of work.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to match speed, accuracy, storage, and versatility with examples from daily life.

topics.title: Disadvantages
topics.content: The textbook also explains limitations and risks of computer use.
learning_points: Computers depend on instructions and data supplied by people.
Long or improper use can affect health and posture.
Personal information can be at risk if it is not protected.
Computers cannot replace human feelings, judgement, and responsibility.
topics.activity_text: Discuss healthy computer habits and why personal information should be protected.

chapters.title: Keyboard and Mouse
chapters.description: Explore keyboard and mouse through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in keyboard and mouse.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Keyboard
topics.content: A keyboard is an input device used to enter letters, numbers, and instructions into a computer.
learning_points: Alphabet keys are used to type letters and words.
Number keys are used to enter numbers.
Special keys include Enter, Spacebar, Backspace, Delete, Shift, Caps Lock, and arrow keys.
The textbook explains how key combinations and punctuation keys are used while typing.
examples: Moves to a new line or confirms.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to locate the alphabet, number, Enter, Spacebar, Backspace, and arrow keys.

topics.title: Mouse
topics.content: A mouse is a pointing device used to move the pointer and interact with items on the screen.
learning_points: The left button is commonly used to select items.
The right button opens a shortcut menu.
The scroll wheel moves a page up and down.
Clicking, double-clicking, dragging, and scrolling are common mouse actions.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate click, double-click, right-click, drag, and scroll using a mouse.

chapters.title: Parts of a Computer
chapters.description: Explore parts of a computer through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in parts of a computer.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Input devices
topics.content: Input devices are used to enter data and instructions into a computer.
learning_points: A keyboard is used to type letters, numbers, and commands.
A mouse is used to point, click, and select.
A microphone records sound.
A scanner sends pictures or documents into the computer.
topics.activity_text: Identify the input devices shown in the textbook and explain what information each one enters.

topics.title: Output devices
topics.content: Output devices show or produce the results processed by a computer.
learning_points: A monitor displays text, pictures, and video.
A printer produces a paper copy called a printout.
Speakers and headphones provide sound.
A projector displays computer output on a larger screen.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to sort the devices into those that show, print, or play computer output.

topics.title: Storage devices
topics.content: Storage devices keep data and information so that it can be used later.
learning_points: A hard disk stores data inside a computer.
A pen drive is a portable storage device.
Memory cards can store photos, videos, and other files.
CDs and DVDs are optical storage media.
topics.activity_text: Show a pen drive or memory card and ask students what kinds of files can be stored on it.

chapters.title: IPO Cycle
chapters.description: Explore ipo cycle through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in ipo cycle.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Working of machines
topics.content: Machines perform work through a sequence of input, process, and output. The chapter illustrates this with familiar examples such as washing clothes and preparing juice.
learning_points: Input is the material or information supplied to a machine.
Process is the work the machine performs on the input.
Output is the result produced by the machine.
A washing machine takes dirty clothes and water as input, washes them, and produces clean clothes.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to identify the input, process, and output in a mixer or washing machine.

topics.title: Working of a computer
topics.content: A computer follows the IPO cycle: Input, Process, and Output.
learning_points: Input devices enter data and instructions.
The CPU processes the data.
Output devices present the result.
For example, when we type using a keyboard, the computer processes the input and displays the result on the monitor.
topics.activity_text: Use a keyboard, CPU, and monitor to demonstrate the IPO cycle in the classroom.

chapters.title: Fun with Tux Paint
chapters.description: Explore fun with tux paint through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in fun with tux paint.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Introduction to Tux Paint
topics.content: Tux Paint is a drawing program that children can use to create pictures using colours, shapes, and drawing tools.
learning_points: Tux Paint provides a drawing canvas.
It includes tools and colours for creating pictures.
The program is designed to make drawing activities enjoyable and easy to explore.
topics.activity_text: Open Tux Paint and let students explore the drawing canvas and colour palette.

topics.title: Tools of Tux Paint
topics.content: Tux Paint provides tools for drawing and editing pictures. The chapter introduces tools such as Paint, Stamp, Lines, Shapes, Text, Magic, Eraser, and Undo.
learning_points: Paint and Lines help create freehand drawings and lines.
Shapes and Stamp add ready-made shapes and pictures.
Text adds words to a drawing.
Eraser removes parts of a drawing.
Undo can reverse the last action.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to find the Paint, Stamp, Shapes, Text, Eraser, and Undo tools and demonstrate one use for each.

topics.title: Open, save, and quit
topics.content: The chapter explains how to open Tux Paint, save a drawing, open a saved drawing, and quit the program.
learning_points: Open Tux Paint from the computer.
Use the Save tool to save your drawing.
Use the Open tool to view a previously saved drawing.
Use Quit when you have finished; save your work before closing.
topics.activity_text: Guide students through creating a small drawing, saving it, opening it again, and quitting Tux Paint.

chapters.title: Sequencing and Decoding
chapters.description: Explore sequencing and decoding through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in sequencing and decoding.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Sequence
topics.content: A sequence is a set of steps or items arranged in a specific order. The chapter uses familiar routines to show why order matters.
learning_points: A sequence tells us what happens first, next, and last.
Daily routines and instructions can be written as sequences.
Changing the order of steps may change the result.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to arrange picture cards for a daily routine in the correct order.

topics.title: Patterns and loops
topics.content: A pattern is something that repeats in a regular way. A loop is an action or set of instructions that repeats.
learning_points: Patterns can repeat colours, shapes, sounds, or movements.
A loop repeats an action or instruction.
Recognising patterns helps us understand repeated steps in computing.
topics.activity_text: Create a repeating colour or shape pattern and ask students to continue it.

topics.title: Decision making
topics.content: Decision making means choosing what to do from different options. The chapter introduces choices and conditions using everyday examples.
learning_points: A decision is a choice between options.
A condition helps decide which action should happen.
For example, we may choose what to do depending on whether a condition is true or false.
topics.activity_text: Give students simple situations, such as choosing what to wear depending on the weather, and discuss the decision.

chapters.title: Instructions and Direction Sense
chapters.description: Explore instructions and direction sense through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in instructions and direction sense.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Instructions
topics.content: Instructions are steps that tell a person or computer what to do. A computer program is made of instructions that guide the computer through a task.
learning_points: A program contains instructions for the computer.
Instructions should be clear and arranged in the correct order.
A sequence of commands can make a character or robot perform a task.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to give clear step-by-step instructions for a simple classroom task.

topics.title: Direction sense
topics.content: The chapter introduces four basic directions used to move objects on a screen: up, down, left, and right.
learning_points: Up moves an object higher on the screen.
Down moves an object lower on the screen.
Left moves an object to the left.
Right moves an object to the right.
Arrow keys can be used to give direction commands.
topics.activity_text: Create a simple grid path and ask students to guide a character using up, down, left, and right commands.

chapters.title: AI and Robotics
chapters.description: Explore ai and robotics through the Foundation 2 textbook lesson and practice activities.
learning_objectives: Understand the main ideas in ai and robotics.
Practise the skills described in the textbook.

topics.title: Introduction to AI
topics.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a way of making machines perform tasks that usually need human intelligence, such as recognising patterns, understanding commands, and making decisions.
learning_points: Voice assistants such as Google Assistant, Siri, and Alexa respond to voice commands.
Face recognition uses a person’s facial features to identify or verify them.
AI is used in everyday devices and services.
The chapter contrasts natural or human intelligence with artificial intelligence.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name a voice assistant or smart feature they have seen and explain what it does.

topics.title: What are robots?
topics.content: A robot is a machine created by people to perform tasks. Robots can be designed for different jobs and may use sensors and instructions to act.
learning_points: Industrial robots help make cars and assemble products.
Medical robots assist in medical work.
Entertainment robots can interact or perform activities.
Military and other specialised robots are designed for particular tasks.
Robots are machines; humans are living beings with feelings and independent human experiences.
topics.activity_text: Match examples of robots with their tasks: assembling, helping in medicine, entertaining, or exploring.
